notes.title: Is _there even interest in this typeee of “different” g_ames?
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=M8X_SNJ8xQ8;full][/previewyoutube]

The issues of today's world are worth pondering. When I consider everything happening around us, it doesn’t exactly fill me with joy. Whether it’s global events or the gaming and entertainment industry. Bukkaku is currently far from completion. I keep wondering if such a complex and problematic development process will ever see the light of day in a form that I would be satisfied with. It’s a challenging project—everything is meticulously hand-drawn and created (take that, fuck AI, my friend), and it stands out artistically. I’m considering the unpopular idea of financial support through a crowdfunding campaign. Will it work? Is there even interest in this type of “different” games? What is the financial threshold or injection required just for visibility? Artistic experimental games no longer have the same boom or interest as they once did. Unfortunately, today there is less and less space for these more unique and personal projects.

[previewyoutube=S8ttW4zcRbs;full][/previewyoutube]

Bukkaku and Ynccuth were never primarily intended as a means of getting rich or making a profit but rather as a form of entertainment and a way to channel my inner creative thoughts. I am also focusing my energy and time on my second dream project—the animated film Ynccuth. Is this the right path? Should I also seek financial support from like-minded individuals? Is there even an interest in an animated film that defies mainstream standards? Will it boost both projects or bury them for good? Ynccuth is a far more personal project. Its atmospheric and emotional core should capture the essence of the film.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42051399/fc5ca4245a778171aed44e808f444feffe4c57ed.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42051399/3fcecee3207107db527b779cee020e593745dbd1.jpg[/img]

 That’s all from my inner battle with the future of the game Bukkaku and the film Ynccuth. Of course, I would appreciate any media mentions. Also, check out other more commercially oriented services, mainly for the Czech Republic, from my digital studio at [url=https://rzestudio.com/]rzestudio.com[/url] Follow my “active” film and game projects through devblogs and keep your fingers crossed for hopefully peaceful years ahead…

notes.title: Complicated creation process
notes.content:
Time passes faster than I thought. The question is how much work I actually have left to do on all my projects. The answer, unfortunately, is quite clear. It's several years. I don't have as much time as I'd like to, and that's due to a job that, while safely covering important financial needs, is not internally fulfilling like my personal projects. I have two long term dream projects in the works that I want to pursue more in the future. An animated film called Ynccuth and a computer game called Bukkaku. In the meantime, I am also working on my RZE studio and my own e-shop wauow.com. I'd like to report on the progress and news in short posts once in a while as well with updates.

[previewyoutube=HOqSggqhznA;full][/previewyoutube]

The maps are designed as a mixture of psychedelic and strongly abstract environments. You move around the map with the character and try to escape from the monsters. In the end, it's quite fun when nothing leads you astray. There will be no character or game settings. No clues or explanations. I hate endless explanations about the game and its name. Try to think with your head sometimes and engage or awaken your creative brain cells. I'll just leave it up to you. Make up your own mind. I will try to finish the playable prototype as soon as possible. I'll let you know what went wrong again and what's new. Thx. Off.

Finally, it's time for some new information about my ever-changing game project with the "interesting" name of Bukkaku. I finally decided to go 3D low poly in a way that makes a lot of sense to this concept from the start. In addition, I also work on the digital e-shop wauow.com and create an animated film Ynccuth. It is a never-ending project that is constantly changing and experimenting with the technical game system. This punk approach will of course also have an impact on the final product. [h2][b]Peekaboo[/b][/h2]

Short animated movie from the Origami world of upcomming indie game Bukkaku. Telling the story of a short life of certain wood creature living in tough world, that after unexpected circumstaces discovers an enormous power inside him self. Live with Bugaboo his story full of terror and pain in magical surface of the Wood or in monster filled depths. "Bugaboo" is a cute creature with terrifying features resembling wraith or monster. 

I was working for over a year on animation. Graphical elements are comming from origami polygonal style and since the begining of game creation i am constantly improving on it and shaping it to detail and more specific image. It is sharp origami angles combined with live colors of Maxican flavor. Short animated horror movie "Peekaboo" is actually supose to symbolize the playful side of the game. Significant part of the game is about hiding and searching.

notes.title: Bukkaku in 3D
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42051399/fbadde00a331d8454eb79487bcc93aba986e52cc.jpg[/img]

It's been a long time since I last reported. A lot of things have changed, so I'd like to update you on what's currently happening with the long-running Bukkaku project, the new Ynccuth movie, and graphic design projects. For the game's problematic project with the "controversial" title, I've been thinking about a total re-working of the game and graphic concept in the last few months. As a perpetually dissatisfied creator, I'd like to tighten the concept up even and define the final fixed points as my ever-changing final idea. For a long time now, this game prototype has been over my head with its ambitious goals. After all, I'm more of a graphic designer than a programmer. I have to say that programming this game is beyond me. For so many years, I've spent my spare time on this project alone, not only doing the graphics, but also programming functional levels, animations or game maps. Yes, it would take a change at last. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42051399/9cf2592b8578791106a1c685b9ac0dd7f1ba1240.jpg[/img]

[b]Problematic and lengthy process[/b]
The experimental game prototype of Bukkaku is a rather long and messy process. From the original naive idea in 2015 as a browser-based MMORPG, it progressed through various experiments with Top-Down view elements and a more action-oriented style to a horror isometric view with a survival story until it reached the 3D dimension in a more predatory colorful Origami "Low poly" design. My previous games have always had a clear vision from start to finish, but unfortunately with Bukkaku I'm still searching for it. This is due to the fact that I'm not happy with the ever-changing outcome, and I'm not sure if this chaotic process will have the outcome I'm hoping for. Hopefully this project can be woken up and completed successfully with a new member...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42051399/6b280f01d5681a919f74917aaedd46226f576249.jpg[/img]

[previewyoutube=rpGKtIrYRQw;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]A dark cinematic story[/b]
I am currently working on my other very interesting project at the same time. It is an animated film called Ynccuth. It's still in development (and will be for a long time) and it's a horror movie with a darker stylization reminiscent of the world of Bukkaku. Just more grown up and thoughtful with a sci-fi vibe. I'm full of ideas on how to bring this dark yet enchanting fantasy world full of monsters and strong characters to life through storytelling.
